label: Diagram 11.2
caption: Diagram 11.2 Relevant boundary
description: The drawing is a diagrammatic plan of a solid-line square labelled 'Building', sides marked A (left), C (top) and B1, B2 (right). Dashed lines around it represent boundaries, each tied to an annotation by a leader line. A left vertical dashed line: 'This boundary coincides with and is therefore relevant to side A'. A right vertical dashed line: 'This boundary is parallel to and therefore relevant to side B1'. A dashed line below the square: 'The boundary is parallel to side B2'. A diagonal dashed line top right, with an angle '< 80°' to a horizontal reference: 'This boundary is at less than 80 degrees to side C and is therefore relevant to side C'. A bottom dash-dot line: 'But the relevant boundary may be the centre line of a road, railway, canal or river'. Top left: 'See para 11.5'. A right-hand NOTES panel says the diagram sets out the rules for a relevant boundary, listing a. Coincide with the side of the building (A); b. Be parallel to the side of the building (B1 or B2); c. Be at an angle of maximum 80 degrees to the side of the building (C). Footer: 'Diagram 11.2 Relevant boundary'.

notes: The description says the square's sides are marked "A (left), C (top) and B1, B2 (right)", but the drawing shows B1 on the right side and B2 on the bottom side, not both on the right.
